```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(phyloseq)

# Here I downloaded the species-level feature table fro the ‘Microbial Composition.qzv file provided by SeqCenter and QIIME2 - Note that Anshul compared this to the Microbial Composition.tsv file provided and the relative abundances calculated each way match 

#Anshul also ran emu to compare the relative abundances of Bifido pseudolongum across samples and it agrees 
#Looked at a few other species and it agrees (Although there is some disagreement with classification ie - Lepagella vs M intestinale (they are closely related at least))




mina_p002_otu <- read.csv("/Users/anshulsinha/Desktop/microbiome_center/projects/005_mina_project_06_2025/P005_02/seq_center_analyses/seq_centre_16S/level-7 (1).csv", header=TRUE)


#if we view the counts table - we can see that samples are the first column, and each other columns indicate unique species found in the data set 
mina_p002_otu


#The last two columns are titled "condition" and "pooled" - we dont need these (they just repeat the sample name ) - we can remove them 

mina_p002_otu_edit <- mina_p002_otu %>% 
  dplyr::select(-condition, -pool)



#For phyloseq, we need the table orientation to be flipped - taxa as rows and sample names as columns 
#To first do this, we need to first set the first column as rownames (this removes the names of the samples)
rownames(mina_p002_otu_edit) <- mina_p002_otu_edit$index
mina_p002_otu_edit$index <- NULL

#now if we look at our counts table, the first column name is gone 
#now to transpose the table (flip columns and rows)
mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed <- t(mina_p002_otu_edit)

as.data.frame(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed)

#convert to a matrix format: 

mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_mat <- as.matrix(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed)

#tells us the dimension of our matrix 
dim(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_mat)

#Lets manually check that things were transposed properly 

mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_mat



```

```{r}
#Now lets create a tax-table where we have a list of our different species and their associated taxonomic designations as columns in a matrix

##NOTE- Double Check the Taxonomy Created from the Qiime2 output -  some names look a bit strange ### 

#we can start with our counts table (transposed)

mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df <- as.data.frame(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed)


#create a column with the full taxonomy 
mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df$taxonomy <- rownames(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df)
rownames(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df) <- NULL

#now just keep that taxonomy column 
mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df <- mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df["taxonomy"]




#now we can separate this into columns based on our taxonomy: 
# Split by period that is followed by a taxonomic prefix (d__, p__, c__, o__, f__, g__, s__)
#results in a list where each element is a vector of 7 parts.


splits <- stringr::str_split(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df$taxonomy, "\\.(?=[dcpofgs]__)")

# Step 2  Convert list to dataframe directly
#rbind() = "row bind" - stacks vectors as rows in a matrix
#do.call() - calls rbind() with the list elements as arguments
#Converts the list of vectors into a matrix where each row = one taxonomy string's parts


df_split_mina_tax <- do.call(rbind, splits) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  setNames(c("Domain", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"))



 # Step 3: Add original taxonomy column back
tax_table_final_mina <- mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df %>%
  bind_cols(df_split_mina_tax)

#some sanity checks here: 
#Is order maintained correctly ?

# Before splitting
original_order <- tax_table_final_mina$taxonomy

# After splitting and binding
final_order <- mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_df$taxonomy

# Check they're identical
identical(original_order, final_order)  # Should return TRUE


#Now lets look at a few rows: the taxonomy column should match the subsequent rows 



tax_table_final_mina
#Now lets double check that our taxonomy split worked: Ie- every "Family" value should start with f and every "Genus" should start with "g"
all(startsWith(tax_table_final_mina$Family, "f__")) #should be TRUE
all(startsWith(tax_table_final_mina$Family, "g__")) #should be FALSE 
all(startsWith(tax_table_final_mina$Genus, "g__")) #should be TRUE 




#Almost there...

# Set the taxonomy column as row names
rownames(tax_table_final_mina) <- tax_table_final_mina$taxonomy

#remove the taxonomy column 
tax_table_final_mina$taxonomy <- NULL


#convert to matrix 
tax_table_final_mina <- as.matrix(tax_table_final_mina)
dim(tax_table_final_mina)
```

```{r}
class(mina_p002_otu_edit_transposed_mat) #should be matrix
class(tax_table_final_mina) #should be matrix 
class(metadata_mina_p002) #should be a data.frame

#convert to format that can be imported by phyloseq
```

```{r}
####FMT EXPERIMENT#####
#What does the stock look like? 

ps_FMT_experiment_stock <- subset_samples(ps_full_MP002, Group=="Stock_PBS" | Group=="Stock_BCG" )


ps_FMT_experiment_stock_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_FMT_experiment_stock, function(x) x / sum(x))

# 2. Melt to long-format data frame (works fine even with 1 sample)
df_FMT_stock <- psmelt(ps_FMT_experiment_stock_rel)

# 3. Order species by descending abundance and drop zero-abundance taxa
df_FMT_stock2 <- df_FMT_stock %>%
  filter(Abundance > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(Abundance)) %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = unique(Species)))

df_FMT_stock2 %>%
  select(Abundance,Genus, Species)

# 4. Plot stacked bar
ggplot(df_FMT_stock2, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Family)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", width = 0.5) +
  ylab("Relative Abundance") +
  xlab(NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())



#Aggregate to family level 
# 1. Same relative abundance transform as before
ps_FMT_experiment_stock_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_FMT_experiment_stock, function(x) x / sum(x))

# 2. Melt to long-format
df_FMT_stock <- psmelt(ps_FMT_experiment_stock_rel)

# 3. Identify top 10 families by total (summed) relative abundance across samples
top10_families <- df_FMT_stock %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(TotalAbundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(TotalAbundance)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  pull(Family)

# 4. Relabel everything outside the top 10 as "Other", then collapse/sum those rows per sample
df_FMT_stock_top10 <- df_FMT_stock %>%
  mutate(Family = ifelse(Family %in% top10_families, as.character(Family), "Other")) %>%
  group_by(Sample, Family) %>%
  summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Family = factor(Family, levels = c(top10_families, "Other")))


df_FMT_stock_top10 <- df_FMT_stock_top10 %>%
  mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = c("FMT_PBS_gDNA", "FMT_BCG_gDNA")))
# 5. Plot stacked bar
ggplot(df_FMT_stock_top10, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Family)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", width = 0.5) +
  ylab("Relative Abundance") +
  xlab(NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())
```

```{r}
sample_sums(ps_full_MP002)
ps_FMT_experiment <- subset_samples(ps_full_MP002, Experiment=="FMT")

library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1234)
ps_rare_FMT <- rarefy_even_depth(
  ps_FMT_experiment,
  sample.size = min(sample_sums(ps_FMT_experiment)),
  rngseed = 1234,
  replace = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

sample_sums(ps_rare_FMT)
ord_bray_fmt <- ordinate(ps_rare_FMT, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")
plot_ordination(ps_rare_FMT, ord_bray_fmt, color = "Group", shape= "FMT_time_point") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  #stat_ellipse(aes(group = Group), linetype = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA of ps_FMT_experiment",
       color = "Group")



#Replot

library(ggplot2)

plot_ordination(
    ps_rare_FMT,
    ord_bray_fmt,
    color = "Group",
    shape = "FMT_time_point"
) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    scale_color_manual(
        values = c(
            BCG_FMT   = "darkorange3",
            PBS_FMT   = "midnightblue",
            Stock_BCG = "red3",
            Stock_PBS = "darkcyan"
        )
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
        panel.grid = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA of ps_FMT_experiment",
        color = "Group",
        shape = "FMT time point"
    )
```


```{r}
#Make a barplot  between FMT and PBS at D2 and D21

ps_FMT_experiment <- subset_samples(ps_full_MP002, Experiment=="FMT")

ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi <- subset_samples(ps_FMT_experiment, Group=="PBS_FMT" | Group=="BCG_FMT")
                                               

ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi <- transform_sample_counts(ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi, function(x) x / sum(x))


# 2. Melt to long-format data frame (works fine even with 1 sample)
ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_df <- psmelt(ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi)

# 3. Order species by descending abundance and drop zero-abundance taxa

fam_df_FMT_experi_df <- ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_df %>%
  group_by(Sample, Group, FMT_time_point, Family) %>%
  summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

##plot the top 10 fam

top10_families <- fam_df_FMT_experi_df %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abundance)) %>%
  slice(1:10) %>%
  pull(Family)

#
library(tidyverse)
fam_top_other <- fam_df_FMT_experi_df %>%
  mutate(
    Family_collapsed = if_else(Family %in% top10_families, as.character(Family), "Other"),
    Family_collapsed = fct_inorder(Family_collapsed)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Sample, Group, FMT_time_point, Family_collapsed) %>%
  summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")


fam_top_other2 <- fam_top_other %>%
  mutate(Sample = as.character(Sample))  # drop global factor levels

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(fam_top_other2,
       aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Family_collapsed)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Group) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))



# T1_DA23 only
fam_T1 <- fam_top_other2 %>%
  filter(FMT_time_point == "T1_DA23")


fam_T1 %>% 
  group_by(Group, Family_collapsed) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance))

ggplot(fam_T1,
       aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Family_collapsed)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Group, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))



# T2_DA23 only
fam_T2 <- fam_top_other2 %>%
  filter(FMT_time_point == "T2_DM14")

fam_T2 %>% 
  group_by(Group, Family_collapsed) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance))

ggplot(fam_T2,
       aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Family_collapsed)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Group, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#Bif rel ab

  group_by(Sample, Group, FMT_time_point) %>%   # add other metadata vars if you like
  summarise(RelAbund = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  filter(FMT_time_point == "T1_DA23")


ggplot(bif_T1,
       aes(x = Group, y = RelAbund)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.6) +
  ylab("Relative abundance of f__Bifidobacteriaceae") +
  theme_bw()

    aes(x = Group, y = RelAbund, fill = Group)
) +

        width = 0.1,
        alpha = 0.6,
```

```{r}


#Now we can save this as the dds with the following formula 
library(DESeq2)

#prune zero sum taxa (ie - taxa not found in any sample)

ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_2_T2_prune <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_2_T2) > 0, ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_2_T2)

sample_sums(ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_2_T2_prune)
sample_data(ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_2_T2_prune)

dds_t2 = phyloseq_to_deseq2(ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_2_T2_prune, ~ Group)


colData(dds_t2) 
#Can add poscounts #NOTE that adding poscounts may have some minor changes on results 
#dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = "poscounts")

#design(dds)
dds_deseq_group_t2 = DESeq(dds_t2, test="Wald") #default DESEQ2 settings

levels(colData(dds_t2)$Group)
resultsNames(dds_deseq_group_t2) #Group_PBS_FMT_vs_BCG_FMT PBS IS THE NUMERATOR!


res_t2 = results(dds_deseq_group_t2, contrast = c("Group", "BCG_FMT", "PBS_FMT"))
summary(res_t2) #42 up in PBS and 31 up in BCG + 2 outliers #this is using the 0.1 cutoff though and no LFC cutoff. Actual will be higher 

res_t2_df <- as.data.frame(res_t2)

sigtable_t2_df_1 <- res_t2_df[res_t2_df$padj < 0.05 & abs(res_t2_df$log2FoldChange) > 1,]
sigtable_t2_df_1
res_t2_df

#now join with the tax_table for all taxa 

table_joined_t2 <- cbind(as(res_t2, "data.frame"), as(phyloseq::tax_table(ps_FMT_experiment_FMT_experi_2_T2_prune)[rownames(res_t2), ], "matrix"))





# Remove rows with NA padj values
table_t2 <- table_joined_t2[!is.na(table_joined_t2$padj), ]

# Ensure unique rownames (EnhancedVolcano uses rownames for matching)
#rownames(table_t2) <- make.unique(table_t2$Species)

# 1. Define colors with simplified nested ifelse
table_t2_keyvals <- ifelse(
  table_t2$log2FoldChange > 1 & table_t2$padj < 0.05, "#FA9442", #increased in BCG group
  ifelse(
    table_t2$log2FoldChange < -1 & table_t2$padj < 0.05, '#06004f', #increased in PBS
    'lightgrey'  # everything else is grey
  )
)

# 2. Replace NAs with grey (not black, since that's our neutral color)
table_t2_keyvals[is.na(table_t2_keyvals)] <- 'grey'

# 3. Name your vector entries to correspond to legend labels
names(table_t2_keyvals) <- ifelse(
  table_t2_keyvals == "#FA9442", 'Enriched in BCG-Vaccinated Donor Group',
  ifelse(table_t2_keyvals == '#06004f', 'Enriched in PBS-control Donor Group',
    'Not significant'  # grey points
  )
)



#check
sigtable_t2_df_2 <- table_t2[table_t2$padj < 0.05 & abs(table_t2$log2FoldChange) > 1,]


sigtable_t2_df_2_BCG <- sigtable_t2_df_2[sigtable_t2_df_2$log2FoldChange > 0,]  #23 increased in BCG donor group 

sigtable_t2_df_3_PBS <- sigtable_t2_df_2[sigtable_t2_df_2$log2FoldChange < 0,] #31 increased in PBS group 

#Export Table 2 

table_t2_export <- table_t2
table_t2_export$direction <- ifelse(
  table_t2_export$log2FoldChange > 1 & table_t2_export$padj < 0.05, "BCG", #increased in BCG group
  ifelse(
    table_t2_export$log2FoldChange < -1 & table_t2_export$padj < 0.05, 'PBS', #increased in PBS
    'Non-significant'  # everything else is grey
  )
)
table(table_t2_export$direction)
write.csv(table_t2_export, "/Users/anshulsinha/Desktop/microbiome_center/projects/005_mina_project_06_2025/P005_02/seq_center_analyses/seq_centre_16S/deseq2/deseq2.csv")

#are other ones significant too? 
table_t2_export
```
